name: Harivarman
dates_notes: A third- to fourth-century placement is conventional, but rests chiefly on the Chinese transmission of the work and later historical reports rather than on a securely dated Indian record.
core_thesis: Harivarman's *Tattvasiddhi* is a substantial early Abhidharma synthesis that rejects important Sarvāstivāda positions, including the three-times existence of dharmas, while developing an analysis of persons and conditioned phenomena. The affiliations proposed for its author and text—Sautrāntika, Dārṣṭāntika, Bahuśrutīya, and Dharmaguptaka—are disputed; the entry therefore presents the treatise rather than assigning Harivarman a settled sectarian identity.

engaged_works.title: Tattvasiddhi
engaged_works.ascription_notes: The work is transmitted under Harivarman's name in the early Chinese translation tradition. Its Indic original is lost; Kumārajīva's Chinese translation (Taishō 1646) is the principal complete witness.
engaged_works.summary: A systematic Abhidharma treatise preserved in Chinese translation. It organizes doctrinal questions around the analysis of dharmas, persons, causal conditions, meditative practice, and liberation, while frequently differing from orthodox Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika interpretations. Any direct reader implementation must work from the Chinese witness or a reliable translation, since no complete Sanskrit text survives.

reception_notes: The text founded the influential Chinese Satyasiddhi school. Its Indian sectarian location remains a problem of reconstruction, so later labels should not be treated as self-descriptions.
